subject: Pinecrest Labs renewal — staged uplift, invoice smoothing, and usage floor proposal
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garner <alex.garner@pinecrestlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pinecrest renewal — staged uplift, invoice smoothing, and usage floor proposal

Alex —

Thanks for taking time during Friday's call. As promised, I pulled together a concrete renewal approach that addresses Pinecrest's concern about near-term budget variability while preserving the unit economics we need to support the committed capacity. High level:

- Term: 12 months (July 1 start) with an option to extend to 24 months at predefined stages.
- Commit cadence: staged uplift — start at 60% of current commit for months 1–3, step to 85% for months 4–9, then 100% for months 10–12.
- Invoice smoothing: monthly amortization of onboarding credits and a 60-day grace window for true-up adjustments to avoid mid-quarter budget shock.
- Usage floor: 50% usage floor on the committed capacity to guarantee a baseline price; unused portion can be banked as credits applied to overages for the next quarter (caps apply).

Attachments: I attached a versioned plan (Pinecrest_MA_plan_v2.xlsx) with the monthly pricing ladder and example invoice scenarios.

Ask: Please confirm if the staged uplift cadence and the invoice-smoothing mechanics are acceptable from a procurement perspective. If so, Ben and I will finalize the price table and issue a DocuSign-ready quote.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0162

From: Alex Garner <alex.garner@pinecrestlabs.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@pinecrestlabs.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pinecrestlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pinecrest renewal — staged uplift, invoice smoothing, and usage floor proposal

Hi Naomi —

Appreciate the clear layout. A few clarifying points from procurement and finance:

1) The staged uplift helps; however, the 50% usage floor on the committed capacity is higher than we expected. Can we look at a 35–40% floor instead?
2) The 60-day grace for true-ups is fine but we need the invoiced amortization to be visible as a separate line item (doesn't help our month-over-month budgeting if it's embedded).
3) We may need an early-exit clause tied to a material breach or unacceptable SLA drops — can redwood include a limited exit right in the first 90 days?

Jordan will lead the procurement validation. If you can share a DocuSign-ready quote and the detailed invoice scenarios, we can run it through our budget owners this week.

Best,
Alex Garner
VP of Product, Pinecrest Labs

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garner <alex.garner@pinecrestlabs.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pinecrest renewal — staged uplift, invoice smoothing, and usage floor proposal

Alex —

Thanks for the quick feedback. Two concessions we can make to close:

- Usage floor: we can move the guaranteed floor to 40% (from 50%) but to protect our economics we would convert the difference into a refundable credit pool that Pinecrest can draw from for overage months within the contract year. The credit pool would be forfeited if Pinecrest terminates for convenience within the first 6 months.
- SLA/exit: we can include a limited 90-day remediation-and-cure exit clause tied to a documented SLA breach event and agreed remediation steps.

I recommend the following minor tweaks to Naomi's spreadsheet before we finalize: label the amortized invoice line clearly as "Onboarding Credit Amortization (monthly)" and add an illustrative month-by-month cashflow tab. I've updated the attached draft quote (DocuSign_Quote_Pinecrest.pdf) for your review.

If that sounds workable, Naomi — can you send the DocuSign link once final? Alex — if procurement signs off on 40% floor + credit pool mechanics, we can lock pricing at today's levels through September (price-hold).

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garner <alex.garner@pinecrestlabs.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@pinecrestlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 14:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pinecrest renewal — staged uplift, invoice smoothing, and usage floor proposal

Alex / Jordan —

Putting the Ben edits into the DocuSign-ready quote now. Key points reflected in the quote and the attached plan:

- Usage floor is 40% with a refundable credit pool equal to the delta between 40% and the original proposed floor. Credits are usable for overages or to offset subsequent quarter invoices per the terms.
- "Onboarding Credit Amortization (monthly)" is an explicit line item with an example amort schedule in the cashflow tab.
- Limited 90-day remediation-and-cure exit right included (documented SLA trigger required).
- Price-hold: we will honor current pricing through 2027-09-30 provided the signed DocuSign is completed by 2027-05-20.

Next steps: if procurement approves, Jordan — please confirm by EOD May 10 and I'll send the DocuSign link; Ben and I will keep the price-hold in effect until May 20.

Thanks —
Naomi

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pinecrestlabs.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Garner <alex.garner@pinecrestlabs.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@pinecrestlabs.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pinecrest renewal — staged uplift, invoice smoothing, and usage floor proposal

Naomi / Ben —

Procurement reviewed and finance ran the month-by-month scenarios. We can accept the 40% floor + refundable credit pool, the separate amortization line item, and the 90-day remediation exit term.

Action items:
- Naomi: please send DocuSign_Quote_Pinecrest.pdf via DocuSign and cc procurement@pinecrestlabs.com.
- Ben: confirm the price-hold through 2027-09-30 as noted.
- Jordan: I will review and countersign once the DocuSign packet is complete (expecting final review within 48 hours).

Appreciate the flexibility — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Regards,
Jordan Lee
Senior Procurement Manager, Pinecrest Labs
